raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When the device (L1) KV pool remains saturated, the allocator currently evicts only the exact token shortfall required by each allocation. Under sustained prefill traffic, this produces many small eviction cycles.

Each cycle synchronously rebuilds and scans the radix-cache eviction heap on the scheduler thread. Once `kv_available_tokens` reaches zero, repeated eviction work stalls the scheduler, introduces pipeline backpressure, and causes a persistent throughput drop even though allocations continue to succeed.

The effect is especially severe for short-input workloads: short requests create allocation and radix-cache activity more frequently while providing less GPU computation over which to amortize the synchronous CPU work.

With an approximately 55-million-token L1 KV pool:

- Sustained 4K input: throughput dropped from approximately 3.62M to 1.90M input tokens/min after saturation (`-47.5%`).
- Sustained 32K input: throughput dropped from approximately 3.82M to 3.63M input tokens/min after saturation (`-5.0%`).

The paged free-list optimization in #37146 reduces release-side metadata overhead, but it does not reduce the number of radix-cache eviction cycles. Profiling shows that the remaining bottleneck is repeated synchronous eviction-heap work.

## Modifications

- Add the opt-in environment variable `SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS`.
- When an allocation first encounters pressure, evict the current shortfall plus a bounded reserve.
- Cap the optional reserve by the number of currently evictable tokens, so headroom cannot turn an otherwise satisfiable allocation into a failure.
- Apply headroom independently to Full KV and SWA KV.
- Preserve no-pressure behavior: no additional eviction occurs while the allocation already fits.
- Keep the default at `0`, preserving exact-shortfall eviction for existing deployments.
- Cover standard, SWA, and unified Full/SWA allocators with CPU unit tests.
- Document the parameter in the environment-variable reference and radix-eviction guide.

This changes eviction batch size, not cache replacement ordering. Reclaimed slots return to the ordinary free pool and remain available to subsequent allocations; they are not permanently reserved.

### Configuration

Set the variable before launching each server process whose L1 KV cache should use batched eviction:

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS=131072 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path MODEL_PATH
```

The value is measured in logical KV token slots, not bytes or pages:

```text
target = shortfall + min(headroom, max(0, evictable_tokens - shortfall))
```

- `0` (default): retain exact-shortfall eviction.
- Positive value: add at most that many evictable token slots when pressure begins.
- Negative value: treated as `0`.
- Full KV and SWA KV calculate their pressure and bounded headroom independently.
- The setting affects L1 device KV eviction only; HiCache/L2 eviction is outside this PR.

For the tested 55-million-token pool, `131072` is about `0.24%` of capacity and `524288` is about `0.95%`. These are workload-specific test points rather than universal defaults. A practical starting point is a small fraction of L1 capacity, followed by validation under sustained saturation.

## Accuracy Tests

This change does not modify model weights, KV contents, page mappings, attention kernels, PD transfer protocols, or replacement ordering. The default is `0`, so existing deployments retain the current behavior unless the optimization is explicitly enabled. Model computation and output accuracy are unchanged.

Added CPU tests cover:

- Default and negative-value exact-shortfall behavior.
- Bounded headroom and evictable-token capping.
- No-pressure behavior.
- Standard L1 KV allocation.
- Independent Full KV/SWA KV handling.
- Unified Full/SWA allocation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### End-to-end saturation test

Environment:

- DeepSeek V4 Pro with PD-disaggregated serving.
- Prefill deployed on two 8xH200 nodes (16 GPUs total).
- PP8/CP2.
- L1 KV pool capacity: approximately 55 million tokens.
- Sustained prefill traffic.
- Optimized runs used `SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS=524288` (approximately `0.95%` of L1 capacity).

| Input length | Exact-shortfall eviction | 524,288-token headroom |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4K | After saturation, throughput fell from approximately 3.62M to 1.90M input tokens/min (`-47.5%`). | The post-saturation throughput cliff disappeared; throughput remained close to its pre-saturation level. |
| 32K | After saturation, throughput fell from approximately 3.82M to 3.63M input tokens/min (`-5.0%`). | Throughput remained stable after saturation. |

The 4K result shows that exact-shortfall eviction is not merely a small steady-state cost: repeated synchronous eviction can consume enough scheduler time to reduce throughput by nearly half. Bounded headroom removes this saturation cliff in the tested short- and long-input workloads.

<!-- Upload the 4K exact-shortfall and 524,288-headroom monitoring screenshots here. -->
<!-- Upload the 32K exact-shortfall and 524,288-headroom monitoring screenshots here. -->

### Detailed 32K profiling

This separate profiling run used a smaller `131072`-token headroom (approximately `0.24%` of L1 capacity) to quantify eviction behavior.

| Metric | Exact-shortfall eviction | 131,072-token headroom | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Throughput before pressure | 64,624 token/s | 64,614 token/s | -0.02% |
| Throughput under pressure | 61,008 token/s | 63,634 token/s | +4.31% |
| Throughput loss after saturation | 5.60% | 1.52% | 72.9% reduction |
| Eviction frequency | 7.45/s | 0.45/s | -93.9% |
| Eviction wall-time share | 2.36% | 0.86% | -63.5% |
| Maximum eviction latency | 337.97 ms | 198.71 ms | -41.2% |
| Allocation failures | 0 | 0 | unchanged |

The optimization leaves pre-pressure throughput unchanged while reducing eviction frequency by `93.9%`. Under sustained pressure, throughput improves by `4.31%`, and saturation-related throughput loss decreases from `5.60%` to `1.52%`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add CPU unit tests for the new behavior.
- [x] Update the environment-variable and radix-eviction documentation.
- [x] Provide end-to-end performance results and eviction profiling.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -14,6 +14,17 @@ The policy scores each candidate and the **lowest score is evicted first**. Once
 
 A policy only scores. It does not decide how much to free, and it cannot pin KV in memory — a node protected by the policy is still evicted if reclaiming everything else is not enough.
 
+## Batch eviction under sustained pressure
+
+By default, SGLang evicts only the token shortfall required by the current allocation. Under sustained KV-pool saturation, this can trigger many small synchronous radix-cache eviction scans. Set `SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS` to reclaim additional L1 KV slots on the first shortfall and amortize that work across later allocations:
+
+```bash Command
+SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS=131072 \
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path MODEL_PATH
+```
+
+The headroom applies only after an allocation no longer fits. It is capped by the currently evictable cache and applied independently to Full KV and SWA KV. Reclaimed slots return to the normal free pool; they are not permanently reserved. The default is `0`, which preserves exact-shortfall eviction. Tune the value against your KV-pool size and workload because a larger value reduces eviction frequency but may reclaim reusable prefixes earlier.
+
 ## Available policies
 
 Select one with `--radix-eviction-policy`. All of them fall back to least-recently-used order within a tie.

+"""CPU tests for bounded L1 KV-cache eviction headroom."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache import common
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.swa import SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.token import TokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.unified_hybrid_swa import (
+    UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import EvictParams
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.common import evict_from_tree_cache
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestKVEvictionHeadroom(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_target_adds_bounded_headroom_only_under_pressure(self):
+        with envs.SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS.override(128):
+            self.assertEqual(common._eviction_target_with_headroom(64), 192)
+            self.assertEqual(common._eviction_target_with_headroom(64, 100), 100)
+            self.assertEqual(common._eviction_target_with_headroom(64, 32), 64)
+            self.assertEqual(common._eviction_target_with_headroom(0, 100), 0)
+
+    def test_zero_headroom_preserves_exact_shortfall(self):
+        for headroom in (0, -1):
+            with envs.SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS.override(headroom):
+                self.assertEqual(common._eviction_target_with_headroom(64, 1000), 64)
+
+    def test_standard_allocator_adds_capped_headroom(self):
+        allocator = object.__new__(TokenToKVPoolAllocator)
+        allocator.available_size = MagicMock(return_value=100)
+        allocator.page_size = 1
+        tree_cache = MagicMock()
+        tree_cache.supports_prefix_sharing.return_value = True
+        tree_cache.evictable_size.return_value = 150
+        tree_cache.token_to_kv_pool_allocator = allocator
+
+        with envs.SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS.override(128):
+            evict_from_tree_cache(tree_cache, num_tokens=200)
+
+        tree_cache.evict_for_alloc.assert_called_once_with(EvictParams(num_tokens=150))
+
+    def test_no_pressure_does_not_evict(self):
+        allocator = object.__new__(TokenToKVPoolAllocator)
+        allocator.available_size = MagicMock(return_value=256)
+        allocator.page_size = 1
+        tree_cache = MagicMock()
+        tree_cache.supports_prefix_sharing.return_value = True
+        tree_cache.token_to_kv_pool_allocator = allocator
+
+        with envs.SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS.override(128):
+            evict_from_tree_cache(tree_cache, num_tokens=200)
+
+        tree_cache.evict_for_alloc.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_swa_adds_headroom_only_to_the_short_pool(self):
+        allocator = SimpleNamespace(
+            full_available_size=MagicMock(return_value=100),
+            swa_available_size=MagicMock(return_value=500),
+        )
+        tree_cache = MagicMock()
+        tree_cache.supports_prefix_sharing.return_value = True
+        tree_cache.full_evictable_size.return_value = 1000
+
+        with envs.SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS.override(128):
+            SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.evict_to_free_tokens(
+                allocator, tree_cache, num_tokens=200
+            )
+
+        tree_cache.evict_for_alloc.assert_called_once_with(
+            EvictParams(num_tokens=228, swa_num_tokens=0)
+        )
+        tree_cache.swa_evictable_size.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_unified_swa_adds_headroom_after_planning(self):
+        allocator = SimpleNamespace(
+            reclaim_plan=MagicMock(return_value=(100, 0)),
+            ensure_capacity=MagicMock(return_value=True),
+        )
+        tree_cache = MagicMock()
+        tree_cache.supports_prefix_sharing.return_value = True
+        tree_cache.full_evictable_size.return_value = 1000
+        tree_cache.swa_evictable_size.return_value = 1000
+
+        with envs.SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS.override(128):
+            ready = UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator.evict_to_free_tokens(
+                allocator, tree_cache, num_tokens=200
+            )
+
+        self.assertTrue(ready)
+        tree_cache.evict.assert_called_once_with(
+            EvictParams(num_tokens=228, swa_num_tokens=0)
+        )
+        allocator.ensure_capacity.assert_called_once_with(200, 200)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

Hi @hzh0425 , sorry for the additional ping. With the holiday approaching, if you have some bandwidth, could you please take a look at this PR? 

It introduces configurable L1 KV-cache eviction headroom to reduce repeated synchronous evictions under sustained cache pressure. The default behavior remains unchanged, while our benchmarks show a significant improvement in post-saturation throughput.

Your review and feedback would be greatly appreciated. No worries if the timing is inconvenient. Thank you!

Hi @hzh0425, thanks for your time!

Quick update: the conflicts with the latest main have been resolved in e70cdba:

- Adopted #39479's switch from evict_for_alloc() to evict() in the unified hybrid-SWA path (so cumulative reclaim quotas are fully honored), while keeping the eviction-headroom reserve applied on top of the reclaim plan.
- Updated the unit-test assertion accordingly, and adapted the mocked guard to the supports_prefix_sharing rename from #42362.

The PR itself is functionally unchanged: a bounded, opt-in (SGLANG_OPT_KV_CACHE_EVICTION_HEADROOM_TOKENS, default 0) L1 eviction headroom that amortizes synchronous radix-cache eviction under sustained saturation — it eliminates the 4K-input throughput cliff (-47.5%) we observed on DeepSeek V4 Pro PD with a ~55M-token pool. With the default of 0, eviction behavior is identical to current main.

I noticed the CI runs so far stopped at the pr-gate check because the PR doesn't carry the run-ci label yet — the test suites never actually started. Would you mind running /tag-run-ci-label (or /run-full-ci) on this PR when you get a chance? And of course, a review of the approach itself would be greatly appreciated — happy to make adjustments based on your feedback. Thanks!

Hi @hnyls2002  @hzh0425 @xiezhq-hermann  , apologies for the follow-up and for tagging multiple reviewers. Since this change touches the core L1 KV-cache eviction path under mem_cache/allocator, could any one of you please help review the implementation or trigger CI when convenient?

This PR addresses repeated synchronous L1 KV-cache eviction scans under sustained cache pressure. The optimization is opt-in, bounded by evictable capacity, and defaults to zero, so existing behavior remains unchanged.

We have repeatedly validated it through internal A/B testing on DeepSeek V4 Pro with two H200 prefill nodes and PP8/CP2. Under sustained 4K prefill traffic, exact-shortfall eviction caused throughput to drop from approximately 3.62M to 1.90M tokens/min after KV-pool saturation. With bounded eviction headroom enabled, this throughput cliff disappeared. Profiling also showed a 93.9% reduction in eviction frequency without affecting pre-pressure throughput.

The currently failed checks are only due to the missing CI label; substantive test jobs have not run yet. Any review feedback or guidance on the next step would be greatly appreciated, and I will address it promptly. Thank you for your time!
